# 0007: well-known types are generated by the user

- Status: accepted, pending the project owner's review. It is cheap to
  change: no generated code depends on it yet.
- Date: 2026-11-04
- Bead: gpb-8qn.5
- Builds on: [0006](0006-naming.md) (naming)

## Question

Protobuf's well-known types (`google/protobuf/any.proto`, `timestamp`,
`duration`, `wrappers`, `empty`, later `struct` and `field_mask`) need Goose
bindings. Do those ship with the runtime, or does each user generate them?

## Decision

**The user generates them, like any other proto.** protoc already carries
the `.proto` files in its include directory, so they need no path:

```sh
protoc --plugin=protoc-gen-goose=... --goose_out=out \
  google/protobuf/duration.proto google/protobuf/timestamp.proto
```

This writes `out/google/protobuf/duration.goose`, in namespace
`google_protobuf`, which a program imports as
`import google.protobuf.duration;` and uses as
`google_protobuf::Duration`. Several such files share the namespace in one
program. The generator has no special case for them.

## Why

- **No version skew.** Generated code and `pb_wire` change together until the
  layout settles. A shipped copy would have to match both the generator and
  the runtime the user has; generated files match by construction.
- **Nothing to release.** Shipping means choosing a package layout and a
  release step, which the runtime distribution spike (gpb-wof.5) has not
  decided. Generated bindings cost none of that and can move into a package
  later without changing their names.
- **Only what is used.** Goose builds whole programs, and each message's
  pools are globals. A program compiles only the types it generated.

## Consequences

- protoc generates only the files named on its command line. Once fields of
  imported types are stored (gpb-8qn.9), a `.proto` that imports
  `google/protobuf/duration.proto` needs that file named too, or the import
  in the generated code fails at `goose build`. The usage guide (gpb-dx9.4)
  has to say so.
- Values have no helpers such as `Any` pack and unpack or time conversions:
  they are ordinary messages. Those are outside the binary wire format's
  scope and could come as a separate library.

## Rejected

- **Ship generated bindings with the runtime.** One less step for the user,
  at the cost of the version skew and release step above. It can be added
  later, once a package exists, if the extra step proves to be a nuisance.
